description: A three-panel composite that mixes two EBSD-derived orientation maps with one channeling-contrast micrograph. (a) is an EBSD RD-IPF texture map (50 µm scale bar) with an IPF colour-triangle key (001, 101, 111) in its top-left corner and printed orientation axes ND, RD//TA, TD; many differently coloured grains are cut by a large black, unindexed band and by an unlabelled long white dashed diagonal line. (b) is the matching KAM map (50 µm scale bar) with a discrete legend Min 0 to Max 5 (blue 0, green 1, yellow 2, orange 3, red 4–5); elevated KAM forms bands flanking the black unindexed path while grain interiors stay near zero. A white dashed rectangle labelled "Fig. c" marks the area magnified in (c). (c) is a grayscale channeling-contrast image (10 µm scale bar; printed metadata 5.10 KX, WD 7.0 mm, EHT 15.00 kV, Signal A = QBSD, 26 Feb 2013) showing region A with fine planar slip bands, region B, a dashed "Grain boundary", two "Slip localization" arrows and three arrows marking "Voids" on that boundary, above a large black crack opening. The group links localized slip/misorientation beside a propagating defect to grain-boundary void chains.

subfigures.description: EBSD RD-IPF texture map, 50 µm scale bar, grains coloured by crystal direction via an IPF triangle key (001/101/111); axes ND, RD//TA, TD printed at left. A large black unindexed band and an unlabelled white dashed diagonal line cross the mapped area. Several grains show internal colour gradients.

KAM map derived from the same EBSD scan, 50 µm scale bar, with a discrete Min 0–Max 5 colour legend (blue 0, green 1, yellow 2, orange 3, red 4–5). High-KAM (green/yellow/red) bands follow the flanks of the black unindexed region; grain interiors are blue (near-zero KAM). A white dashed rectangle labelled 'Fig. c' outlines the region shown in (c).

Grayscale electron channelling contrast micrograph, 10 µm scale bar, header reads 5.10 KX, WD 7.0 mm, EHT 15.00 kV, Signal A = QBSD, Date 26 Feb 2013. A dashed 'Grain boundary' line separates region A (fine planar slip bands, two arrows labelled 'Slip localization') from region B; three arrows mark 'Voids' sitting on the boundary, above a large black crack region at the bottom.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an EBSD inverse pole figure map (RD-IPF) with a 50 µm scale bar, colour-coding grains according to the IPF triangle key (001, 101, 111) printed in its top-left corner.
Orientation reference axes labelled ND, RD//TA and TD are printed at the left of panel (a).
A large black, unindexed region cuts diagonally through the mapped area of both (a) and (b), surrounded by colour-coded grains.
Panel (b) is a KAM map with a discrete 0–5 colour legend (blue 0, green 1, yellow 2, orange 3, red 4–5) and a 50 µm scale bar.

In (b) the elevated KAM values (green, yellow, orange, red) are concentrated in bands along the edges of the black unindexed region, while the interiors of the large grains remain blue, i.e. KAM near 0.
A white dashed rectangle labelled 'Fig. c' inside panel (b) delimits the area reproduced at higher magnification in panel (c).
An unlabelled long white dashed diagonal line runs across panel (a) and continues into (b); the caption does not identify it.
Panel (c) carries printed acquisition metadata: 5.10 KX magnification, WD 7.0 mm, EHT 15.00 kV, Signal A = QBSD, Date 26 Feb 2013, with a 10 µm scale bar.
In (c) a dashed line labelled 'Grain boundary' separates region A from region B, and three arrows mark dark 'Voids' located on that boundary above a large black crack region.
Two arrows labelled 'Slip localization' in (c) point at coarse planar slip bands within region A, whereas region B shows a finer lamellar contrast.
The caption states that KAM values were calculated using the first neighbouring EBSD point shell at a spacing of 300 nm.

The caption describes (c) as an 'Orientation optimized ECCI' image corresponding to the part surrounded by white lines in (b), while the metadata printed inside the image give the signal as QBSD; the two statements about the imaging mode do not match and both are reported here as printed.

The citing text states that embrittlement in this alloy involved two mechanisms: cracking at grain-boundary triple junctions, and gradual formation of chains of microvoids on grain boundaries under pronounced planar slip localization, with void coalescence leading to intergranular cracking.
The citing text attributes the intense slip localization to the presence of kappa-carbides in this steel (printed as 'j-carbides' in the source text).
The figure data are stated in the caption to be taken from Ref. 59.

measured_quantities: kernel average misorientation (KAM), legend scale Min 0 to Max 5 (unit not printed on the map)
EBSD neighbour-shell spacing, 300 nm (stated in caption)
scale bar, 50 µm (panels a and b)
EHT / accelerating voltage, 15.00 kV (panel c metadata)

panel (b): the KAM colour legend is printed only as 'Min 0' to 'Max 5' with no unit, so the misorientation scale cannot be read in degrees
panel (c): the phase/composition identity of the fine lamellar contrast in region B is not labelled
panel (c): whether the imaging mode is ECCI (caption) or QBSD (printed metadata) cannot be resolved from the pixels
